newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister begins army phonetap inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister begins army phonetap inquiry.

text.p: Turkey's new interior minister started an investigation on Wednesday into allegations that a senior security official had organised phone-tapping of senior military leaders, state-run Anatolian news agency said.
The allegations follow months of conflict between the secularist military and the outgoing Islamist-led government, which collapsed last month under the strain of the dispute.
The probe order was one of the first actions taken by Interior Minister Murat Basesgioglu since he took over the post from a member of the Islamist-led coalition earlier this week.
Anatolian said Basesgioglu had initiated a probe into Bulent Orakoglu, former deputy head of intelligence at police headquarters.
Orakoglu, who was sent last week to the United States on a one-year posting, has been ordered back to Turkey since the allegations came to light.
Turkish newspapers said the phone-tapping was part of a wider attempt by the security services to spy on the military.

Former interior minister Meral Aksener said in comments to reporters that she had acted appropriately during her time in office and said there should be an enquiry if the security apparatus had overstepped its jurisdiction.
"I did what was necessary during my time in office. Our friend the new minister will do his duty. The independent judge will do what is necessary," she was quoted as saying by Anatolian.
